sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: La Ciotat is a coastal town where parking is a summer problem as much as a daily one. Everything we could source on the street rules comes from the tourist office, which is a secondary source, so we cannot say which municipal decision sets them. Per its page, last modified on 13 August 2026, zone 1 (La Tasse, Pétanque, Escalet and Sandral car parks plus centre-town streets) is paid all year from 8am to 8pm with two hours free once a day, at 3.80 euros for one hour, 7.60 for two and 38 for ten hours [0]. Zone 2, covering the Mugel and Figuerolles car parks and streets near the beaches, is paid only from 1 May to 30 September, 9am to 8pm, with one hour free once a day [1]. The post-parking charge is 38 euros, equal to the ten-hour rate, and the page does not say when this was set [2]. The Calanques National Park strongly advises against driving into the town centre because of heavy visitor numbers and suggests leaving the car at a car park such as Mugel, warning that these are not always supervised; it lists the Ciotabus line 30 to the Mugel and Figuerolles calanques [5]. The city's own website blocks automated access, so we have no municipal source.

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The Métropole Aix-Marseille-Provence announced on 6 December 2023 a temporary offer of two free hours between 10am and 7pm in several metropolitan car parks, including La Ciotat's Vieux-Port and Centre Verdun, on three December weekends to encourage Christmas shopping [7]. A new 249-space car park opened on 9 November 2020 at the La Ciotat-Ceyreste station, managed by RTM and free for stays up to seven consecutive days until the station renovation ended; this is the 2020 position and current terms were not checked [8].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The tourist office lists 15 car parks. La Tasse has 257 spaces, paid 8am to 8pm all year with two hours free; Bérouard has 69 blue-zone spaces, free with a disc for up to 1h30; the Port de Plaisance has 255 spaces, paid from 1 May to 30 September and free from 1 October to 30 April [3]. We found no readable source on the concessions or on who runs the Vieux-Port and Verdun car parks.

Our data cover four car parks with about 1,600 spaces from the Aix-Marseille-Provence feed. Three of them have usable histories, measured since 24 September 2026: Centre (470 spaces), Verdun (295) and the Port de Plaisance (254). Together they averaged about 65% on weekdays and 68% at weekends, weighted by spaces, which makes them among the fuller car parks in our set even outside the summer. Centre averaged 78% and reached full in a single Wednesday-morning reading; Verdun averaged 64% on weekdays and 67% at weekends and also reached full once; the Port de Plaisance, free after 30 September according to the tourist office, averaged 40% on weekdays and 53% at weekends. The Vieux-Port car park (580) shows only one early reading. These are about four weeks of data after the main season.
